# HomeWork 1:
# Given the data, perform the turning point test and check whether accept H0 or reject it.

# Creating Sequence Vector:
seq = c(3, 8, 5, 7, 6, 4, 9, 2)

# Defining length of the sequence:
n = length(seq)

# Initialize u to calculate number of turning points: 
u = 0
for (i in 2:(n-1)){
  # Calculating peek and trough
  if((seq[i-1] < seq[i] & seq[i] > seq[i+1]) || (seq[i-1] > seq[i] & seq[i] < seq[i+1])){
    u = u+1
  }
}

# Under H0, Calculating E(p) and V(p):

expectation_p = (2*(n-2))/3
variance_p = (16*n-29)/90

p = u

# Calculating Z:
Z = (p - expectation_p)/sqrt(variance_p)

# Calculating Z-score:
Z_score = qnorm(1-(0.05/2))

if(abs(Z) > Z_score){
  print("Reject H0")
}else{
  print("Accept H0")
}



# HomeWork 2:

library(fpp3)
ACF

data("vic_elec")

# Inspect the dataset
head(vic_elec)

# Check for missing values
sum(is.na(vic_elec$Demand))

# Trend test:

# Impute missing values using the mean (or other suitable methods)
vic_elec$Demand[is.na(vic_elec$Demand)] <- mean(vic_elec$Demand, na.rm = TRUE)

# Aggregate data to monthly demand
monthly_demand <- vic_elec %>%
  index_by(month = yearmonth(Time)) %>%
  summarize(monthly_demand = sum(Demand))

# Convert 'month' to a numeric sequence representing the order of the months
monthly_demand$month_numeric <- as.numeric(monthly_demand$month)

# Function to calculate Kendall's Tau
kendalls_tau <- function(x, y) {
  n <- length(x)
  concordant <- 0
  discordant <- 0
  
  for (i in 1:(n-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):n) {
      # Check for concordance/discordance
      if ((x[i] < x[j] && y[i] < y[j]) || (x[i] > x[j] && y[i] > y[j])) {
        concordant <- concordant + 1
      } else if ((x[i] < x[j] && y[i] > y[j]) || (x[i] > x[j] && y[i] < y[j])) {
        discordant <- discordant + 1
      }
    }
  }
  
  tau <- (concordant - discordant) / (concordant + discordant)
  return(tau)
}

# Apply the function to our data
tau_value <- kendalls_tau(monthly_demand$month_numeric, monthly_demand$monthly_demand)
tau_value

# Normal approximation of the variance of Tau
n <- length(monthly_demand$month_numeric)
var_tau <- (2 * (2 * n + 5)) / (9 * n * (n - 1))

# Compute the Z-score
z_score <- tau_value / sqrt(var_tau)

# Compute the p-value
p_value <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_score)))

# Print results
cat("Kendall's Tau:", tau_value, "\n")
cat("Z-score:", z_score, "\n")
cat("p-value:", p_value, "\n")


if(p_value < 0.05){
  cat("Reject the null hypothesis\n")
} else {
  cat("Fail to reject the null hypothesis\n")
}

# Seasonality test:

# Since no increasing or decreasing trend was detected, we can directly jump to rank the observations:

# Aggregate data to monthly demand
monthly_demand <- vic_elec %>%
  index_by(year_month = yearmonth(Time)) %>%
  summarize(monthly_demand = sum(Demand))

# Extract year and month
monthly_demand <- monthly_demand %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(year_month),
    month = month(year_month)
  )

# Rank the observations within each year
monthly_demand <- monthly_demand %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(month_rank = rank(monthly_demand)) %>%
  ungroup()

head(monthly_demand)

# Calculate M_i for each month
M_i <- monthly_demand %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarize(M_i = sum(month_rank))

print(M_i)

# Number of years and months
r <- length(unique(monthly_demand$year))
c <- length(unique(monthly_demand$month))

# Calculate X
X <- (12 / (r * c * (c + 1))) * sum((M_i$M_i - r * (c + 1) / 2)^2)
print(X)

# Degrees of freedom
df <- c - 1

# Critical value from chi-square distribution
chi_square_critical <- qchisq(0.95, df)
print(chi_square_critical)

# Compare X with chi-square critical value
if(X > chi_square_critical) {
  cat("Reject the null hypothesis: There is seasonality in the data.\n")
} else {
  cat("Fail to reject the null hypothesis: No significant seasonality detected.\n")
}


# Turning point test:

# Aggregate data to monthly demand
monthly_demand <- vic_elec %>%
  index_by(year_month = yearmonth(Time)) %>%
  summarize(monthly_demand = sum(Demand))

# Convert 'year_month' to a numeric sequence representing time order
monthly_demand$time <- 1:nrow(monthly_demand)

head(monthly_demand)

# Calculate turning points
n <- nrow(monthly_demand)
U <- rep(0, n)

for (i in 2:(n-1)) {
  if ((monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i] > monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i-1]) & 
      (monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i] > monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i+1])) {
    U[i] <- 1  # Peak
  } else if ((monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i] < monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i-1]) & 
             (monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i] < monthly_demand$monthly_demand[i+1])) {
    U[i] <- 1  # Trough
  }
}

# Number of turning points
p <- sum(U)
cat("Number of turning points:", p, "\n")

# Expected value of p under H0
E_p <- (2 * (n - 2)) / 3

# Variance of p under H0
V_p <- (16 * n - 29) / 90

cat("Expected number of turning points:", E_p, "\n")
cat("Variance of turning points:", V_p, "\n")

# Calculate Z-score
Z <- (p - E_p) / sqrt(V_p)
cat("Z-score:", Z, "\n")

# Calculate the p-value
p_value <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(Z)))

cat("p-value:", p_value, "\n")

# Make the decision
if(p_value < 0.05) {
  cat("Reject the null hypothesis: The series is not random.\n")
} else {
  cat("Fail to reject the null hypothesis: The series is random.\n")
}
